text: Azure Data Factory's Copy activity copies data from a source to a sink. For Overlook, the source is a daily export file the scheduling system drops into Blob Storage, and the sink is the Appointments table in OverlookDB.

Regardless of source or sink, the Copy activity always does the same three things: reads from the source, performs serialization and column mapping, and writes to the sink. Both ends of this specific pipeline — Blob Storage and Azure SQL — are reachable from Data Factory's own Azure Integration Runtime, with no self-hosted runtime needed.

The pipeline itself is simple by design: a scheduled export file mapped into the Appointments table, with fault tolerance skipping incompatible rows into an error log rather than failing the whole run.

The Copy activity handles extract and load well, but it's deliberately limited on heavier transformation — which this modest appointment feed doesn't actually need. Next lesson covers monitoring this pipeline, so a failed run gets noticed the same way Chapter 5's health checks get noticed.
